lacuna.current_status: Sweep run 2026-09-15 against the 2026-09-07 corpus freeze. (1) vLLM: v0.29.0 released 2026-09-09 (two days post-freeze); its headline is Model Runner V2 (MRV2) now default for ALL models (#53183), i.e. upstream's 'V2' execution/scheduler stack completed its rollout; also padded FULL-cudagraph dispatch for uniform decode under spec decode (#53407), batch-sharded sampling cutting per-step logits memory by 1/TP (#50465, TP2-relevant), 'widest uniform decode batch captured by default' (#50488), per-arch tuned batch-invariant matmul configs (~3x on decode kernels, RTX 4090D/H20, #53247), FlashInfer XQA falls back on unsupported head_dim (#53111), a KVCacheLayout enum standardization (#51718), and queue admission control (#49445). v0.28.0 (2026-08-26) carried the item most adjacent to this host: a fused CUDA post-conv MTP decode kernel for Qwen3.5 GDN (#51674) plus 'GDN gates aligned with speculative tokens' (#51812) - upstream fused the exact GDN-draft step this host measured as non-compounding on its own champion (MEMORY.md 2026-09-13/14: MTP x champion dead at family scale; stock K1 inversion 1.32/1.13 vs champion 1.06/0.87). v0.28 also: max_num_batched_tokens 8192->16384 (#51726), a CI-guarded GPU<->CPU sync elimination campaign (#43107, #51458...). Merged sm75-touching PRs in the window are maintenance-grade only: #43914 fp8>=sm89 arch enforcement (2026-06-15), #45176 Marlin to torch stable ABI (2026-06-12), #45375 modelopt_mixed enabled on Turing (2026-06-23), #46550 SM75 topk-histogram build fix (2026-06-24), #48438 Marlin weight-reload storage fix (2026-07-30), #39878 default CUDA 13.0 + arch list cleanup (2026-04-23). No new sm75 attention or decode kernel landed upstream vLLM in the window. (2) FlashInfer: THE sm75 delta of the window. PR #3526 'fix: keep HEAD_DIM 256 prefill within 64 KiB smem on SM75/SM70' merged 2026-07-22, shipped in v0.6.16 (2026-07-31) - this is the host's exact recorded breakage (#3620-class 64 KiB smem overflow) at the host's exact head dim d256. Releases since: v0.6.17 (2026-08-11), v0.6.18 (2026-08-29), v0.6.18.post1 (2026-09-05, the version vLLM now pins). v0.6.16's headline content is otherwise Blackwell-first: MegaMoE expert-parallel kernels (SM100+, NVSHMEM), MiniMax sparse attention on SM120/121, XQA decode extensions (sliding window, sinks, ragged Q for spec decode) on SM120/121. vLLM PR #55380 '[Turing] Restore flashinfer support for SM75' (opened 2026-09-04, draft 2026-09-11, ready 2026-09-12, new commits 2026-09-14) is STILL OPEN as of 2026-09-15: it lowers vLLM's FlashInfer floor back to SM75 on top of FlashInfer 0.6.16+, states 'head dimensions above 256 are unsupported on SM75' (64 KiB opt-in smem ceiling - d256 is the last supported dim), and adds an SM75-only warning to uninstall flashinfer-jit-cache (the JIT-cache wheel dropped Turing kernels). So 'v0.23.0 last-good FlashInfer-sm75' is now one unmerged PR away from being superseded. [uncertain] Note on anchors: host records cite #45375 as the deliberate v0.24.0 FlashInfer-sm75 drop; that number currently resolves to '[Quant] Enable modelopt_mixed on Turing (SM75)' merged 2026-06-23 (inside the v0.24.0 window, released 2026-06-29) - either the drop rode a different PR or the same PR did double duty; unresolved. (3) DeepGEMM: 2026-04-16 public release (PR #304): 'Mega MoE, FP8xFP4 GEMM, FP4 Indexer, PDL, faster JIT' - SM90/SM100 tensor-core paths (FP8/FP4); nothing reachable from cc 7.5 (no FP8/FP4 MMA on Turing; W4A16 Marlin remains the host's lane, upstream Marlin changes in the window are ABI/maintenance). (4) FlashMLA: [uncertain, secondary sourcing] early-2026 activity reported as next-gen-model support and Blackwell optimizations; releases API lists no tagged releases. MLA is a deprioritized family for this host (CONSOLIDATION T10) - record only as ecosystem signal. (5) TRT-LLM: open-source line is v1.3.0rc* (rc15 2026-05-21 ... rc26 2026-09-09); rc26 highlights: DeepSeek-V4 Hopper (#16940), Qwen3.8-Flash-Next support (#18585 - the host's model family, Flash-Next native MTP head), Rubin SM107 GEMM/MoE/CuTe-DSL, trtllm-gen FMHA kernel+cubin refresh (#18183), SkipSoftmax sparse attention (#17781). Known-issues list flags FlashInfer-backend memory growth. No cc 7.5 / pre-Ampere kernel drops surfaced in the window [uncertain: full support-matrix diff not performed]; the drop pattern remains Blackwell-cubin-first (trtllm-gen cubins are arch-specific), confirming old silicon lives on vLLM/Triton/llama.cpp paths, not TRT-LLM. (6) llama.cpp: v0.4.1 tagged 2026-09-14; the 'decode-graph restructuring' is the CUDA-graph line, still open-PR as of 2026-09-15: #16548 'Implement and use cuda graph plans' (opened 2025-10-13, open), #27721 'CUDA graphs on Pascal (sm_61): +40% on MoE, +7% on dense, no regression' (opened 2026-08-25, open), #26771 'Recapture graph after memory pool flush' (2026-08-08, open), #28549 'Enable CUDA graph for MTP draft' (2026-09-07, open). The Pascal datapoint is the window's cleanest old-silicon scheduling result: graph capture alone worth +7-40% e2e on 2016 silicon. Mirage/MPK megakernel-compiler line continues (CMU/Stanford). Nothing in the FlashDecoding++/megakernel lineage targets or ports to cc 7.5 in this window.
lacuna.applicability: Transfers: (a) FlashInfer #3526 (merged 2026-07-22) + vLLM #55380 (open): the sm75 prefill smem hole the bridge kernel was recorded as filling now has an upstream fix at exactly d256; when #55380 merges, the host gains a second maintained backend to A/B as control arm and loses some urgency from the 'bridge fills the FlashInfer hole' differentiation - but the restore PR's own text constrains d<=256 on SM75, so the host's d256 shape sits on the boundary and any future d growth is closed to FlashInfer anyway. Probe cost on merge: hours (vllm_ab_run.py control-arm swap). (b) Upstream's fused Qwen3.5-GDN MTP decode kernels (#51674 v0.28, #52539 v0.29 'all Qwen head ratios') are the concrete mechanism behind the measured stock-K1 inversion (MEMORY.md 2026-09-14): kernel-count reduction on the draft path is what makes MTP pay on this engine class - directly relevant to the host's 'past-the-floor-via-MTP needs a graphs-compatible mechanism' open item, as a named upstream implementation to read at the next rebase. (c) MRV2-default (#53183) means the host's V1-era engine fork diverges from upstream's execution stack each rebase window - CONSOLIDATION T1's rebase verdicts (dense REBASE, MoE REBASE+absorb, attention DIVERGE) should be re-struck against MRV2, not V1, at the next rebase. (d) FlashDecoding++Next's unified-max idea (fixed/common max to skip the split-combine rescale pass) ports to ANY silicon and is the only paper-line mechanism that touches the host's split walk+combine structure; its numeric risk (flat-max overflow/underflow class) rhymes with the host's fp16 tie-break adjudication class (MEMORY.md 2026-09-14 gate lesson). Not transferable: DeepGEMM MegaMoE/FP8xFP4/PDL and FlashInfer MegaMoE/XQA/MSA (SM90/SM100/SM120 tensor-core or NVSHMEM features absent on TU102); TRT-LLM trtllm-gen cubins (arch-specific Blackwell); Ada-MK/megakernel line (demonstrated on SM89+, and a whole-step megakernel collides with the host's 2-resident-CTA occupancy law and conflicted STS halves - persistent cross-tile scheduling on sm_75 has no cp.async/TMA to hide the staging). Net: the March-September 2026 delta contains NO new sm75-capable decode-kernel SoTA; the incumbent pressure on the host's numbers is unchanged, and the actionable items are ecosystem (FlashInfer restore watch, MRV2 rebase surface, GDN-MTP fusion precedent), not kernel surgery.

design.mechanism: Doctrine + watch items, no new kernel mechanism to implement cold. (1) Watch vLLM #55380; on merge, run the existing interleaved A/B harness (vllm_ab_run.py) with FlashInfer as a third arm at ctx512/ctx2048 batch 4-8 on the d256 hybrid - d256 is the sm75 ceiling per the PR text, so this A/B stays valid permanently; record FlashInfer vs TRITON vs bridge in the champion ledger. (2) At the next engine rebase, diff upstream MRV2's decode step structure (uniform-batch FULL cudagraph dispatch #53407, widest-batch capture #50488, batch-sharded sampling #50465) against the host's V1 fork - these three are exactly the step-scheduling surfaces plan/0010's step-profile ledger measures; adopt any that shrink inter-kernel gaps on sm_75 (all are graph-structure changes, cc-agnostic). (3) Read upstream #51674/#52539 (fused Qwen3.5 GDN MTP decode) as the implementation precedent for a graphs-compatible MTP mechanism on the GDN side; the host's own MTP verdicts say the win comes from removing draft-path kernel launches, which is a fusion boundary decision, portable to the host's GDN kernels without tensor-core dependence. (4) If the split-combine pair is ever re-opened after the chrome-trace inversion is root-caused, FlashDecoding++Next's unified-max (choose a shared max per (row, head) from seq stats, skip the L2-rescale in the combine kernel) is the one paper mechanism that deletes combine-kernel work rather than moving it; gate it on the existing greedy 3/3 canary discipline. (5) Re-affirm in the corpus: no sm75 decode-kernel SoTA landed March-September 2026; DeepGEMM/FlashMLA/TRT-LLM/FlashInfer headline work is SM90/SM100/SM120-only.
design.failure_modes: (a) Ecosystem drift, not kernel failure: #55380 has code-owner reviews pending and was force-pushed once already (2026-09-12) - do not pre-adopt from the PR branch; the JIT-cache wheel also dropped Turing kernels, so a FlashInfer arm must JIT-compile locally (the PR's warning commit exists precisely because stale cached cubins break Turing). (b) Unified-max numerics: a shared max breaks when one segment's scores are extreme (long-tail KV); defense is the host's gate-0 greedy-identity canary plus per-row max fallback - this is the same fp16 tie-break adjudication terrain the host already mapped (MEMORY.md 2026-09-14: mean worst-row 0.004 class), do not let a benign adjudication launder a real distribution shift. (c) MRV2 adoption on the fork is an engine-lane rebase cost, not a free pull: the host's d256 kernel API lives adjacent to vendored FA2 trees (T1 history), and MRV2 changes metadata plumbing those shims touch. (d) False-positive pressure: the llama.cpp Pascal graphs result (+7% dense) is pre-Turing and MoE-heavy; do not project its magnitude onto the host's already-graphed decode step. (e) [uncertain] FlashMLA status rests on secondary sourcing (Baike/aggregators); no tagged releases to cite - do not propagate it as fact into other records.
design.effort_estimate: Doctrine-only now (this record + CONSOLIDATION delta lines); engine-lane probe of a few hours when #55380 merges (A/B harness exists); MRV2 rebase assessment rides the already-planned next rebase window, +0.5 day to re-strike T1 verdicts; GDN-MTP upstream read, half a day. No kernel-lane days.
design.priority_signal: Against the sensitivity floor (only multi-ms per-step deltas move rows): NONE of the window's items projects a multi-ms delta on the host's step - the sm75 kernel landscape is static, so this item cannot close the ~4.3 ms and should not queue kernel surgery. Its load is risk-shaping: (1) HIGH-value watch: FlashInfer-sm75 restore changes which backends the 'ecosystem abandoning this silicon' doctrine argument covers (MEMORY.md 2026-09-09 doctrine explicitly hangs production-target status on TRITON being an ecosystem-backed baseline; a restored FlashInfer arm strengthens that insurance at zero kernel cost); (2) MODERATE: MRV2-default is the largest engine-structure divergence since the host forked and lands exactly on the step-scheduling surfaces this research run targets - it belongs in the next rebase decision, not this one; (3) LOW: GDN-MTP fusion precedent matters only if the operator re-opens the MTP lane that two windows of A/Bs closed. Recommended disposition: bank as doctrine + two named watch items (PR #55380, MRV2 rebase), no milestone tasks created from it now.
